recipes.title: Baked Piroshki
recipes.intro: Soft yeasted buns stuffed with beef, onion and dill. A sample recipe to show how a recipe with several ingredient groups looks.

Dough: 3 1/2 cups flour, plus more for dusting

steps: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and leave it for 5 minutes until foamy.
Whisk in the egg, melted butter and salt, then add the flour a cup at a time until a soft dough forms.
Knead for about 8 minutes until smooth and a little tacky. Cover and let it rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Meanwhile, soften the onion in the butter over medium heat, about 8 minutes. Add the beef, salt and pepper and cook, breaking it up, until browned. Stir in the dill and let it cool.
Punch the dough down and divide it into 16 pieces. Flatten each into a 4-inch round.
Put a heaped tablespoon of filling in the middle of each round, fold it over and pinch the edges firmly to seal. Set them seam-side down on a lined baking sheet.
Cover and let them rest for 15 minutes while the oven heats to 375°F (190°C).
Brush with the egg wash and bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until deep golden.
recipes.notes: They freeze well after baking. Reheat from frozen at 350°F for about 15 minutes.

recipes.title: Lemon Bars
recipes.intro: A sample recipe with no serving count, so the page offers batch sizes instead.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line an 8-inch square pan with parchment.
Mix the crust ingredients into a crumbly dough, press it into the pan and bake for 18 minutes.
Whisk the filling together and pour it over the hot crust.
Bake for another 20 to 22 minutes, until just set. Cool completely, dust with powdered sugar and cut into squares.
